question.text: The magnetic intensity at the centre of a long current carrying solenoid is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the number of turns is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn></math> per <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>, then the current flowing through the solenoid is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
The magnetic intensity H is defined as the product of the number of turns per unit length in a coil n and the current that it carries I.

The magnetic field of a solenoid is given by B=μ0ni

H=Bμ0=μ0niμ0⇒H=ni   ...(i) 

The given data is 

H=1.6×103 A m-1

n=8 per cm

Substituting the values in equation (i)

⇒1.6×1000=81100×i

⇒i=2 A
